name: Čatež Bridge over the Sava
zag_role: Combined earthquake and flood vulnerability assessment
description: Within the CROSScade project the bridge was selected as the most critical of seven bridges studied, two of them in Slovenia near the Brežice hydropower plant and the others near Zagreb. Reasons given were its role on a key regional route, the lack of adequate scour protection and a design that predates modern performance-based seismic provisions. The first half of the bridge was modelled in Midas Civil and OpenSeesPy with soil-structure interaction, and fragility curves were derived for sequential ground shaking, flood loading and local pier scour.
history: The Čatež bridge carries a regional road across the Sava close to the Slovenia to Croatia border. It is a 12 span prestressed reinforced concrete girder bridge, 359.8 m long, designed in the mid 1970s. It is divided into four brake units by expansion joints. The intermediate piers are pairs of 1.2 m circular columns on bored piles, while piers 5 and 9 are transverse reinforced concrete walls on a pile cap with six inclined piles.
facts: non-linear time-history, earthquake followed by flood and scour
